A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe Mosaic3D and Mosaic3D-5.6M. The main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D support comparison despite relocated references and renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation benchmarks, pipeline ablations, model-scaling experiments, text-encoder comparisons and ScanRefer results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds dataset-quality measurements, class-name anonymization results and outdoor qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The data engine, SparseUNet/Mask3D architecture, caption merging and two-stage training are retained. However, the rewritten contrastive losses have different temperature and pooling expressions. The PDFs do not resolve whether these differences represent equation errors or actual changes to the training objectives.

E1.justification: v2 adds two ETH3D outdoor attention examples and training-data comparisons using LEO, MMScan and EmbodiedScan. Coverage expands through alternate language supervision and a limited outdoor test; the five Mosaic3D source datasets and quantitative benchmark tasks remain unchanged. ScanRefer was already evaluated in v1 Appendix C.3.

E2.justification: New Table 4 and Appendix Table A2 substantially broaden dataset-based comparisons, evaluating LEO, EmbodiedScan, MMScan and SceneVerse alongside RegionPLC and OV3D supervision. These are training-data baselines evaluated with a shared model architecture. Comparator membership in the existing Tables 1–3 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces class-name anonymization in training captions, with architecture, CLIP model and loss held fixed across comparisons (Table 4). Appendix Table A2 adds controlled dataset comparisons and measures unique normalized nouns, captioned-point coverage and entropy of ground-truth instance IDs within masks. Existing benchmark splits and stated training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses quantify caption diversity and mask quality (Figure 2 and Appendix A.1), test dependence on explicit class names (Table 4), and examine indoor-to-outdoor transfer (Figure 7). The existing pipeline, model-scaling, text-encoder, ScanRefer and category-frequency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for these experiments. The added results continue using point estimates; the new mask-entropy measure assesses annotation quality rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial dataset-quality and anonymization results; Table 4 reports Mosaic3D-5.6M at 15.7 f-mIoU without anonymization and 10.5 with it. Table 2 revises decoder mAP50 from 6.4 to 7.0, mAP25 from 8.7 to 12.3, and head/common/tail mAP from 6.1/3.5/1.7 to 6.6/2.1/2.8, while overall mAP remains 3.9. Tables 1, 3 and the retained appendix result tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: The printed loss definitions change beyond equivalent notation: v1 Equations 4 and 7 apply temperature in both numerator and denominator, whereas v2 Equations 2 and 5 omit denominator temperature. v2 also expands masked pooling into a mask-weighted sum despite prose describing averaging. These introduce mathematical inconsistencies; no new theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an automatically generated 5.6M-pair dataset, a language-aligned encoder with a lightweight decoder, the first single-stage open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation without ground-truth labels, and state-of-the-art segmentation results. The revised foundation-model terminology does not materially alter these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes annotation-free evaluation from its stricter class-name-anonymized zero-shot setting and interprets outdoor attention as transfer from indoor training. It also uses direct caption/mask measurements to support dataset-quality interpretations. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit sparse-view limitation and proposed remedy through synthesized views.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link in the abstract. Existing preprocessing instructions, checkpoints, captioning prompts, filtering thresholds, training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused discussion of 3D vision-language datasets and contrasts their dependence on human annotations with Mosaic3D's automatic pipeline. Seven works are newly cited, including ReferIt3D, ScanQA, LEO, MMScan, EmbodiedScan, ETH3D and V-Net; one earlier citation is removed. The central novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting. Semantic and instance segmentation related work are merged, dataset-related discussion is introduced, Section 5.4 becomes a broader Analysis section, and references move before the supplement. Most existing appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4 and Appendix Table A2, redraws Figure 2 with quantitative annotations, and revises Figure 7 to include outdoor examples. Figure 5 notation and Figure 6 labels also change. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and repositioned, while the appendix qualitative figures and overall two-column design are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 4's class-name anonymization test and Table A2's dataset-quality and shared-model comparisons strengthen support for the dataset contribution beyond v1's benchmarks and ablations. These gains are tempered by ambiguities introduced into the loss equations and removal of the explicit sparse-view limitation, yielding a limited net improvement.
